account:
Today has mostly looked like ordinary town business, though I still have a feeling I am missing something. The only unusual lead is talk of lights at the bakery and the baker carrying a sack of bread near the bridge. The neighbour mentioned the lights, but did not personally witness the baker's journey; their account of the bread came from Townsfolk Ten. I do not know which way the baker was going or whether anyone accompanied them. The baker said the bread was fresh stock for market, not for a special occasion. The secretary has heard no reports of shortages or unusual evening activity. This could simply be normal baking and market deliveries; I have no evidence of a secret gathering or other hidden purpose.

At the afternoon accounts meeting, the builder reported no confirmed defects at the bridge, landing, or warehouse approach, and no spending. Freight said the warehouse was empty and there were no confirmed orders, and offered delivery and ferry services if an authorized job arose. Those seem like people seeking ordinary work, not evidence of unusual activity. I verified 128 emeralds in the treasury, but outstanding commitments remain unverified because the secretary has not seen an accounts ledger. No spending was authorized. The innkeeper came to the meeting, but I could not make out their business, so that remains unknown.

I have now arrived a little late for three o'clock tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage. The neighbour is here with three townsfolk nearby. This is an opportunity to listen for local news and ask what, if anything, the neighbour actually knows about the bakery lights, without treating rumours as established facts. I must return to the office for my 16:30 appointment.
